# Note: the pathing assumes you start in the root "blume-capel-analysis".

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
setwd(here::here())

library("haven")
library("tidyverse")
library(clipr)
library(brms)

source("./scripts/preprocessing.R")
source("./scripts/lazy-functions-v2.R")

priors <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = b),
  prior(normal(0, 1.5), class = Intercept),
  prior(exponential(1), class = sd)
)

priors_null <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1.5), class = Intercept),
  prior(exponential(1), class = sd)
)

print(priors)
print(priors_null)
```

# Null model (intercept only)

```{r null-model}
invisible(capture.output(
  bay_mid_null <- brm(
    mid_success ~ 1 + (1 | pseudo),
    data = all_changes,
    family = bernoulli(link = "logit"),
    prior = priors_null,
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
    seed = 42,
    cores = 11,
    refresh = 0,
    file = "scripts/manipulation/all-attitudes/brm-models/bay_mid_null"
  )
))
print(summary(bay_mid_null))
```

For each model, a summary is printed to inspect which of the 95% confidence intervals contain zero. Those that do not contain zero
indicate plausible estimates for that predictor.

# Full model (all predictors)

```{r all-predictors-model}
invisible(capture.output(
  bay_mid_all_pred <- brm(
    mid_success ~ Condition + imp_scaled + knw_scaled + pol_scaled + (1 |
                                                                        pseudo),
    data = all_changes,
    family = bernoulli(link = "logit"),
    prior = priors,
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
    seed = 42,
    cores = 11,
    refresh = 0,
    file = "scripts/manipulation/all-attitudes/brm-models/bay_mid_all_pred"
  )
))
print(summary(bay_mid_all_pred))
```

Unfortunately, though, no model is more likely than the null, not even close, even though the priors are very forgiving.

# Model comparison

```{r model-comparison}
all_bayes_models <- bayestestR::bayesfactor_models(
  bay_mid_null,
  bay_mid_cond,
  bay_mid_imp,
  bay_mid_knw,
  bay_mid_pol,
  bay_mid_cond_imp,
  bay_mid_cond_knw,
  bay_mid_cond_pol,
  bay_mid_all_pred
)

print(all_bayes_models)

bf_inclusion <- bayestestR::bayesfactor_inclusion(all_bayes_models)
print(bf_inclusion)
```

---

Still, let's ask the question:

People who were *not* at the midpoint at T1 — did they end up there at T2?

```{r switchers-data}
all_mid_switchers <- all_changes %>%
  filter(pre_mid == 0)
```

```{r switchers-null}
invisible(capture.output(
  bay_switch_null1 <- brm(
    mid_success ~ 1 + (1 | pseudo),
    data = all_mid_switchers,
    family = bernoulli(link = "logit"),
    prior = priors_null,
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
    seed = 42,
    cores = 11,
    refresh = 0,
    file = "scripts/manipulation/all-attitudes/brm-models/bay_switch_null1"
  )
))
print(summary(bay_switch_null1))
```

```{r switchers-full}
invisible(capture.output(
  all_bayes_switch1 <- brm(
    mid_success ~ Condition + imp_scaled + knw_scaled + pol_scaled + (1 |
                                                                        pseudo),
    data = all_mid_switchers,
    family = bernoulli(link = "logit"),
    prior = priors,
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
    seed = 42,
    cores = 11,
    refresh = 0,
    file = "scripts/manipulation/all-attitudes/brm-models/all_bayes_switch1"
  )
))

summary(all_bayes_switch1)
bayestestR::bayesfactor_parameters(all_bayes_switch1)

invisible(capture.output(
  bay_switch_BF1 <- bayes_factor(all_bayes_switch1, bay_switch_null1)
))
```

The answer is still "no".

```{r switchers-BF}
print(bay_switch_BF1)
```
